title: Mathematics on arXiv — latest batch: 9 October 2026
global_caveat: arXiv publishes no official trending chart; this is an editorial inference based on claimed mathematical results, scope, cross-subfield relevance and limited independent attention. Papers are only days old, so citation evidence is sparse and ordering is not a popularity measure.

sections.title: Global asymptotic stability of homogeneous polynomial vector fields is undecidable
sections.abstract: The authors study whether one can decide global asymptotic stability of the origin for homogeneous polynomial vector fields with rational coefficients and prove undecidability in fixed degree and dimension settings.
sections.claimed_result: The authors reduce undecidable integer-equation questions to global stability and show many-one completeness for every odd degree at least three when dimension is sufficiently large; cubic stability is undecidable in a fixed dimension.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Homogeneous polynomial vector fields over rational coefficients; the theorem concerns stability of the origin. The sufficient dimension is not stated as a minimal threshold.
sections.unique_caveat: The fixed-dimension corollary does not identify the smallest dimension; it is a new preprint.

sections.title: Characterization and scaling limit of three-dimensional loop-erased random walk and random-walk loop-catchers
sections.abstract: A Brownian-loop-soup recovery property uniquely characterizes the three-dimensional loop-erased random walk (LERW) scaling limit, resolving the 3D case of a Sapozhnikov–Shiraishi conjecture, and the authors construct 3D Brownian loop-catchers.
sections.claimed_result: In a bounded connected Lipschitz domain in three dimensions, the intensity-one loop-soup recovery property determines a unique law, which is the scaling-limit law of LERW in the unparametrized Hausdorff trace topology; the authors also construct 3D Brownian loop-catchers.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A bounded connected Lipschitz domain in R^3 containing the origin; the recovery property uses an independent intensity-one Brownian loop soup and Brownian motion stopped at the domain boundary.
sections.unique_caveat: The characterization and construction are for three dimensions and the stated domain/recovery setup; they do not settle analogous laws in every dimension.

sections.title: The Kakeya problem for codimension-two planes in R^n
sections.abstract: For n >= 4, the authors prove near-maximal volume bounds for unions of codimension-two plane neighborhoods satisfying convex Wolff-type nonconcentration, with an application to a curvature-restricted four-dimensional two-plane Kakeya problem.
sections.claimed_result: Under convex Wolff axioms the union of a sufficiently nonconcentrated and sufficiently dense family of delta-neighborhoods of (n-2)-plane segments has almost maximal volume; in n=4 this resolves Rogers' two-plane problem subject to curvature conditions.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: n >= 4, small scale delta, convex nonconcentration and dense shading; the four-dimensional consequence has additional curvature conditions.
sections.unique_caveat: This is not an unconditional resolution of all Kakeya conjectures; the result is hypothesis-dependent.

sections.title: Sharp Polynomial Upper Bounds for Anticanonical Volumes
sections.abstract: For every dimension n, the authors prove a polynomial upper bound for anticanonical volumes of epsilon-lc log Fano varieties with an exponent that is optimal in all dimensions n >= 2.
sections.claimed_result: The authors show vol(-K_X) <= C_n epsilon^-(2^n-n-1) for an n-dimensional variety with an epsilon-lc log Fano boundary; the exponent cannot be decreased for n >= 2, and the optimal fourfold exponent is 11.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Varieties over C; X is normal projective Q-Gorenstein with an effective boundary making it epsilon-lc and log Fano. The constant C_n depends only on dimension.
sections.unique_caveat: The exponent is sharp but the leading constant is not optimized; the estimate is parameterized by epsilon and dimension.

sections.title: Further bounds in the polynomial Szemerédi theorem
sections.abstract: Every sufficiently dense subset of {1,...,N} contains a nontrivial pattern (x, x+y, x+2y, x+y^3), giving a quantitative bound for a configuration of positive complexity.
sections.claimed_result: For some c > 0, any subset of {1,...,N} of size much larger than N/exp((log log log N)^c) contains the displayed pattern.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Finite subsets of {1,...,N} with the displayed density lower bound; one specified polynomial configuration.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract gives a bound for this configuration, not a general quantitative solution of the polynomial Szemeredi theorem.

sections.title: Strong RSW estimates for the FK-Ising model on s-embeddings
sections.abstract: The authors prove strong Russo-Seymour-Welsh crossing estimates for FK-Ising on s-embeddings under a uniformly bounded geometry assumption.
sections.claimed_result: The paper adapts induction over scales for strong RSW crossings of rough topological quadrilaterals with unfavorable boundary conditions, and derives consequences such as quasi-multiplicativity of arm events.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: FK-Ising on s-embeddings whose tangential quadrilaterals have uniformly bounded geometry: edge lengths comparable to one and angles bounded below.
sections.unique_caveat: The result is conditional on uniformly bounded geometry; broader settings are not claimed.

sections.title: The moduli space of curves of genus 16 is uniruled
sections.abstract: Using non-abelian Brill-Noether theory, the authors show that the moduli space of curves of genus 16 is uniruled, the highest genus for which they say this is known.
sections.claimed_result: The authors establish uniruledness of the genus-16 moduli space using non-abelian Brill-Noether theory.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: The object is the moduli space of curves of genus 16; the abstract states no additional hypotheses.
sections.unique_caveat: The abstract claims uniruledness and highest-known-genus status, not a classification for all higher-genus moduli spaces.

sections.title: The sharp L^2-Michael–Simon inequality
sections.abstract: For isometrically immersed n-manifolds in Euclidean space with n >= 3, the authors prove the sharp L^2-Michael–Simon inequality and characterize equality cases.
sections.claimed_result: For every isometric immersion j:(Sigma^n,g)->R^N with n >= 3, a weighted Dirichlet energy with mean-curvature term bounds the Sobolev L^(2n/(n-2)) norm using the sharp constant n(n-2)Vol(S^n)^(2/n)/4; equality cases are characterized.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: Isometric immersion of an n-dimensional manifold into Euclidean space, n >= 3, and u in W^{1,2}(Sigma).
sections.unique_caveat: The theorem concerns the stated Sobolev/mean-curvature inequality and its equality case; it does not claim a general classification of immersed submanifolds.

sections.title: Formally Certifying the Vertex Set of a Polyhedron Faster than Informal Enumeration
sections.abstract: The authors present a proof-assistant-verified certificate for completeness of a polyhedron's vertex list and report their extracted checker is typically 1.5x to over 5x faster than lrslib on tested examples.
sections.claimed_result: They prove correctness of a completeness criterion based on an abstract simplicial complex and implement it in Rocq; experiments include Birkhoff polytopes, cubes and permutahedra.
sections.assumptions_and_setting: A proposed vertex list for a polyhedron given by linear inequalities; the proof checker verifies completeness or exactness.
sections.unique_caveat: The speed comparison is empirical on tested examples and is not a universal runtime guarantee.
